title: Op-amp burns out above its supply rating or when its output carries more than its short-circuit rating

implements.text: The amplifier latches burnt when the voltage between its supply pins passes the absolute maximum, or when its output carries more than the maximum short-circuit current for 100 ms

mocked.text: Once the rule fires the part stays burnt until it is repaired; the real part may survive or fail more slowly

unsupported.text: Thermal history and ageing; only the thresholds and the dwell are checked

parameterSources.note: absolute maximum ratings, supply voltage, LM358
no source; chosen so the inrush into a capacitor behind the output does not burn the part

validation.dataset: src/sim/analog/live-health.test.ts: an op-amp and a 555 in the live solver

operatingRange.evidence: twice the 32 V supply rating of the LM358
twice the 60 mA short-circuit rating of the LM358

knownFailureCases: The model has no output current limit, so a hard short to ground reads 70 mA at 5 V and burns the part; the real LM358 limits near 40 mA and survives a short to ground at 15 V or less
The 100 ms dwell has no source
